conceptZh: 魔術師兔子變魔術，字的筆畫一直從邊邊偷溜進來又躲開，最後被帽子吸住，兔子跳出門「出去」。
object: a cartoon magician rabbit in a purple top hat with a short wand, and a small toy door that stands on the floor
morph: stroke pieces of the glyph 去 keep peeking in from the frame edges and dodging the rabbit before settling in the right places
creativeAngle: 躲貓貓：筆畫從畫面邊緣探頭、躲開魔術師，最後魔法失靈卻剛好歸位；「出去」用兔子跳出小門的動作呼應。
promptEn: An 8-second bright cartoon clip on a clean solid pale lavender backdrop, with one large Traditional Chinese glyph 去 as the only text, built of thick glossy saturated tomato-red strokes, about 70% of frame height, centered with margins. Lead: a cartoon magician rabbit in a purple top hat whose tricks always misfire in a harmless, funnier way; one supporting prop, a small toy door standing at the side. No background music, no subtitles, no vocabulary text. Voice: warm, friendly off-screen narrator in clear Taiwanese Mandarin saying exactly 去、去、出去 (ㄑㄩˋ、ㄑㄩˋ、ㄔㄨ ㄑㄩˋ), slowly with clear tones, then stop. Moment 1 (0–1.8s): the rabbit hops to center, taps his wand on the hat with a flourish, and as the first 去 is spoken the top horizontal stroke and the short vertical peek in from the top-left corner like shy puppies, then duck back out of sight. Moment 2 (1.8–3.6s): the rabbit whips around, wand pointed, and the lower hooking piece peeks in from the right, sticks out its tongue-shaped tip, and slides away every time he reaches for it; he leaps, grabs thin air, and lands flat on his belly, ears pooling over his eyes. Moment 3 (3.6–5s): he tries one more spell, the hat belches a puff of pink smoke, and all the strokes zoom in at once, dodge around him, then plop into place as the second 去 is spoken: a horizontal bar over a short cross stroke above a wide open base with a diagonal tail on the lower right. Moment 4 (5s): the word 出去 is spoken as the rabbit scoots to the little door, flings it open, and hops out in one bouncy leap, returns with his head poking back in, waves, then out again. Final 5–8s: the glyph 去 stays perfectly still and fully legible while the rabbit pops the door open and peeks out, wobbling his hat on his ears with a satisfied grin, never touching the strokes. Soft daylight, no flashing, no real people, no other text.

conceptZh: 橡膠恐龍想抓住一塊溜走的筆畫，小短手怎麼伸都抓不到，只能用大腳追著它滿場繞圈、滑倒、跌倒，最後飛撲肚子落地「啪」一聲，背上的三根筆畫震落疊成「土」，壓在肚子下的小鉤子彈出來停在下面，剛好組成「去」。然後暈頭轉向的恐龍乖乖「回去」自己的小墊子。
object: a runaway bottom hook-piece of the glyph zipping around the floor, chased by a rubber dinosaur balancing three stiff stroke-bars on its back
morph: the dinosaur's belly-flop impact shakes the three bars off its back so they land stacked as the upper 土 part (short horizontal, vertical through it, longer horizontal), while the caught hook-piece squirts out from under its belly and settles below as the 厶 base with its dot, completing 去
creativeAngle: 全新追逐型肢體喜劇，與上一版魔術兔完全不同：恐龍的小短手「抓不到」是整段笑點的引擎，所有動作都靠大腳和整個身體完成，最後用飛撲肚子落地的撞擊把筆畫震成字形，筆畫落點與「去」的結構一一對應。語詞改用「回去」，恐龍在字完成後搖搖晃晃走回起點墊子，聲音與畫面同一個故事，且每個字只有單一讀音。
promptEn: An 8-second bright cartoon chase on a clean solid pale mint backdrop, soft even daylight, no background music, no subtitles, no vocabulary text. The only text ever on screen is one large Traditional Chinese glyph 去 in thick glossy saturated royal-blue strokes, finished at about 70% of frame height, centered with clear margins. Lead: a squishy orange rubber dinosaur with enormous flat feet and comically tiny arms that cannot reach anything, so it does everything with its whole body; it is eager, stubborn and cheerful. Supporting prop: one small royal-blue hook-shaped stroke piece (the 厶 base of the glyph, with its little dot riding on its back) that behaves like a quick cheeky rubber critter. Three stiff blue bars (the strokes of the upper 土 part) ride stacked on the dinosaur's back the whole time. Voice: a warm, friendly off-screen narrator in clear Taiwanese Mandarin says exactly 去、去、回去 (ㄑㄩˋ、ㄑㄩˋ、ㄏㄨㄟˊ ㄑㄩˋ), reading exactly those syllables slowly with clear tones, a short pause between each, then stops. Moment 1 (0–1.5s): the dinosaur stands on a tiny round doormat at the left edge, staring down at the hook piece wiggling at its feet; it strains its stubby arms toward it, misses by a mile, tries bending over and nearly tips, and as the first 去 is spoken the hook piece sticks out a tongue-like tip and zips off to the right across the floor. Moment 2 (1.5–3.5s): the dinosaur thunders after it, huge feet slapping, bars bouncing on its back; the piece zigzags in a wide loop around the frame, the dinosaur skids around a corner on one foot, trips over its own giant toes, somersaults, pops upright with crossed eyes and keeps running in an even bigger loop. Moment 3 (3.5–5s): the piece darts to the exact center and freezes; the dinosaur crouches, wiggles its tail, a one-beat frozen stare, then launches into a huge flying leap and belly-flops with a cartoon SPLAT, squashing wide and flat. As the second 去 is spoken the impact shakes the three bars off its back and they land stacked above it in order: a short horizontal, a vertical dropping through its middle, then a longer horizontal beneath, while the caught hook piece squirts out from under its belly and settles below as the 厶 base with its dot on the right, completing a correctly formed 去. The dinosaur rolls off to the lower left, away from the strokes. Final hold (5–8s): the glyph 去 stays perfectly still, centered and fully legible. At 5.3s the word 回去 is spoken exactly as the dizzy dinosaur stands, wobbles, and waddles back leftward to its little doormat, plops down on it with a satisfied grin and waves one tiny arm, never touching or covering the strokes. Bright but not neon, no white blowouts, no flashing, no real people, no other text, no watermark.
